commonMisinterpretations: Mild hypoxia does not uniformly impair all tasks dose and acclimatization matter.

name: Traumatic Brain Injury Burden
definition: The severity and persistence of functional neurological effects attributable to traumatic injury of the brain.
representationScale: continuous or ordinal level; clinically meaningful thresholds only where validated
polarityDirection: Higher values = greater traumatic brain injury burden.
mechanism: Neurometabolic, vestibular, sensory, sleep, and network disturbances can affect cognition and symptom tolerance. Diffuse/focal neural injury can impair executive functions, memory, inhibition, social cognition, and motor systems.
likelyDownstreamInfluences: Headache, slowed processing, attention/memory problems, fatigue, dizziness, irritability recovery is usually favorable but variable. Executive dysfunction, impulsivity, memory problems, reduced initiation, motor limitations.
moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Symptoms overlap with pain, sleep, stress, and vestibular dysfunction. Profiles vary greatly by lesion, recovery, premorbid function, and rehabilitation.
typicalInteractionCandidates: Interacts with sleep, pain, vestibular function, stress, work demands, and information load. Interacts with social support, rehabilitation, substance use, institutions, and technology aids.
persistenceRecovery: Commonly persists across Days–months; recovery depends on cause, dose, and intervention.
measurementAssessmentMethods: See linked Operationalizations records.
measurementCaveats: Indicators may be state-, protocol-, dose-, and population-dependent; do not equate a single proxy with the construct. Do not infer permanent impairment from concussion prognosis varies and many recover fully. Avoid treating TBI as a uniform personality change.
evidenceNotes: Complex learning, multitasking, or high-stimulation environments may need temporary modification. Do not infer permanent impairment from concussion prognosis varies and many recover fully. Behavior change may require external structure, cueing, simplified choices, repetition, and caregiver/system support. Avoid treating TBI as a uniform personality change.
commonMisinterpretations: Do not infer permanent impairment from concussion prognosis varies and many recover fully. Avoid treating TBI as a uniform personality change.

name: Vestibular Stability
definition: The current level, severity, or functional status of vestibular stability, represented as a variable rather than as a fixed label or diagnosis.
representationScale: continuous or ordinal level; clinically meaningful thresholds only where validated
polarityDirection: Higher values = greater vestibular stability.
mechanism: Vestibular signals interact with visual, proprioceptive, autonomic, and hippocampal systems supporting balance and spatial cognition.
likelyDownstreamInfluences: Dizziness, nausea, avoidance of movement, balance problems, and visuospatial cognitive difficulty.
moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Effects vary across vestibular disorders cognitive evidence is largely associative.
typicalInteractionCandidates: Interacts with technology/VR, transportation, visual environment, anxiety, and nausea.
timeScaleQualifier: May fluctuate episodically over minutes or reflect a chronic vestibular deficit.
persistenceRecovery: Commonly persists across Minutes–chronic; recovery depends on cause, dose, and intervention.
measurementAssessmentMethods: See linked Operationalizations records.
measurementCaveats: Indicators may be state-, protocol-, dose-, and population-dependent; do not equate a single proxy with the construct. Separate vestibular effects from anxiety, hearing loss, medication, and age.
evidenceNotes: Can strongly constrain travel, training environments, virtual-reality exposure, and tasks requiring movement or spatial orientation. Separate vestibular effects from anxiety, hearing loss, medication, and age.
commonMisinterpretations: Separate vestibular effects from anxiety, hearing loss, medication, and age.

name: Agreeableness
definition: A relatively enduring tendency toward compassion, respectfulness, trust, and cooperative interpersonal behavior.
representationScale: Validated broad trait score with compassion and respectfulness facets
polarityDirection: Higher values = greater typical cooperativeness and interpersonal concern.
mechanism: Biases trust, conflict response, helping, and willingness to accommodate others.
moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Situation strength, role demands, culture, age, measurement breadth, current state, and person-situation fit.
persistenceRecovery: Relatively enduring across years, while momentary expression remains situation-dependent.
measurementAssessmentMethods: Validated trait inventories; informant reports; longitudinal assessment; aggregated behavioral indicators
measurementCaveats: Trait scores are probabilistic, instrument-dependent summaries; short forms and cross-cultural use can reduce reliability or equivalence.
evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC202; SRC203.

name: Ambiguity Aversion
family: Decision Valuation Across Risk, Time & Effort
definition: The degree to which options with unknown or imprecise probabilities are valued less than comparable options with known probabilities.
representationScale: Choice premium; ambiguity-aversion parameter; low–high scale
polarityDirection: Higher values = stronger avoidance of probability ambiguity.
mechanism: Adds a subjective penalty to options whose outcome probabilities are unclear.
moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Domain, wealth or resource state, experience, numeracy, affect, time pressure, and elicitation method.
persistenceRecovery: Can shift with framing and state; stable individual differences are only partly persistent.
measurementAssessmentMethods: Incentivized or hypothetical choice tasks; adaptive titration; model-based parameter estimation; structured self-report
measurementCaveats: Estimated parameters can be task-, domain-, stake-, and model-dependent; descriptive regularities are not fixed universal traits.
evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC189; SRC123.
commonMisinterpretations: Treating named biases as immutable defects or assuming one parameter estimated in one task transfers unchanged to all decisions.

name: Anger Intensity

polarityDirection: Higher values = more intense anger.

measurementCaveats: Emotion labels, intensity, and expression vary across people and cultures; self-report, behavior, and physiology need not converge.
evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC115; SRC176.
commonMisinterpretations: Assigning a universal behavioral direction to an emotion; the same emotion can support different actions under different appraisals.

polarityDirection: Higher values = greater expected regret associated with the specified choice or omission.

moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Goal conflict, feasibility, autonomy, feedback quality, time horizon, identity relevance, and opportunity.
persistenceRecovery: Usually reversible as cues, resources, or interpretations change; repeated appraisal can stabilize.

measurementCaveats: Motivation is action- and context-specific; stated goals and intentions can overpredict behavior when opportunity or control is weak.
evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC140; SRC141.
commonMisinterpretations: Collapsing intrinsic, autonomous, controlled, approach, and avoidance motivation into a single amount of motivation.

measurementAssessmentMethods: Use a validated construct-specific instrument, administrative or sensor measure, or transparent composite with explicit unit and reference period.
measurementCaveats: Feasible With Explicit Unit; proxy measures require construct-validity review.

commonMisinterpretations: Do not treat Institutional Trust as interchangeable with PSY-021; PSY-023; PSY-118 or as a universal, context-free cause.

mechanism: Raises the burden on contributors and can reduce cooperation through inequity, pessimistic expectations, or retaliatory withdrawal.

evidenceNotes: Supported by converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, network, or longitudinal evidence. Specific effects and causal interpretation remain conditional on level, context, boundary, and measurement. Representative records: SRC238; SRC261; SRC267.

measurementAssessmentMethods: Use a validated construct-specific instrument, administrative or sensor measure, or transparent composite with explicit unit and reference period.
measurementCaveats: Feasible With Explicit Unit; proxy measures require construct-validity review.
evidenceNotes: Dependency concentration is a structural cause of correlated outages, distinct from current availability and generic interoperability.
commonMisinterpretations: Do not treat Technical Single-Point-of-Failure Concentration as interchangeable with TEC-011; TEC-008; ENV-089 or as a universal, context-free cause.

name: Third-Party Behavioral Observability
definition: Technological capacity for organizations, authorities, or other actors to monitor behavior at scale.
representationScale: Explicit categorical configuration plus attribute-specific dimensions
polarityDirection: Higher values = greater third-party behavioral observability or more of the specified capability.
mechanism: Perceived observability changes expected costs and reputational or sanction consequences, potentially producing compliance or chilling effects.
moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Perceived detection probability, sanction severity, legitimacy, anonymity.
persistenceRecovery: Logs may persist; feedback can be transient
indicators: Public-space cameras alter behavior when people believe activity can be identified and reviewed.
measurementAssessmentMethods: System configuration audit; telemetry or event logs; benchmark testing; controlled interface experiment; technical inspection; structured user testing
measurementCaveats: Technical availability or configuration may differ from actual exposure and perceived affordance; logs may be incomplete; implementation and context moderate effects.
evidenceNotes: Representative evidence supports behavioral relevance, but effects are conditional and heterogeneous. Substantial surveillance literature exists, but effects vary strongly by setting and perceived consequences.
commonMisinterpretations: Treating third-party behavioral observability as a universal behavioral effect, or confusing the technical property with the user’s perception or response.

polarityDirection: Higher values = greater user-activity visibility affordance or more of the specified capability.

measurementAssessmentMethods: System configuration audit; telemetry or event logs; benchmark testing; controlled interface experiment; technical inspection; structured user testing
measurementCaveats: Technical availability or configuration may differ from actual exposure and perceived affordance; logs may be incomplete; implementation and context moderate effects.

commonMisinterpretations: Treating user-activity visibility affordance as a universal behavioral effect, or confusing the technical property with the user’s perception or response.
